{{nihongo|'''Uwase Shrine'''|宇波西神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Wakasa Province]].

'''Uwase Shrine''' (うわせじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} at 129-5 Teradani, Kiyama, {{ill|Wakasa, Fukui|Q1349039|qid=Q1349039}}, {{ill|Mikatakaminaka District, Fukui|Q1204541|qid=Q1204541}}, {{ill|Fukui Prefecture|Q133879|qid=Q133879}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}} ({{ill|Myōjin Taisha|Q9610964|qid=Q9610964}}).

=== Enshrined deity ===
* {{ill|Ugayafukiaezu|Q1373935|qid=Q1373935|lt=Hikonagisatake Ugayafukiaezu-no-Mikoto}} (うがやふきあわせずのみこと)

At nearby {{ill|Wakasahiko Shrine|Q11616630|qid=Q11616630}}, his parent deities {{ill|Hoori|Q1051960|qid=Q1051960|lt=Hikohohodemi-no-Mikoto}} and {{ill|Toyotama-hime|de|Toyotama-hime|es|Toyotama-hime|fa|تویوتاما-هیمه|fi|Otohime|fr|Otohime|id|Toyotama-hime|ja|トヨタマヒメ|ko|도요타마히메|mni|ꯇꯣꯌꯣꯇꯃ-ꯍꯤꯃꯦ|pl|Toyotama-hime|ru|Тоётама-химэ|simple|Toyotama-hime|sv|Otohime|uk|Тойотама-хіме|vi|Toyotama-hime|zh|豐玉毘賣命|qid=Q2329261|lt=Toyotama-hime-no-Mikoto}} are enshrined.

=== History ===
=== Tradition ===
According to tradition, it was founded on March 8, {{ill|701|ab|701|af|701|am|701 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|701|ar|701|ary|701|arz|701|ast|701|az|701|azb|۷۰۱ (میلادی)|ban|701|bar|701|be|701|be_x_old|701|bg|701|bn|৭০১|bpy|মারি ৭০১|br|701|bs|701.|ca|701|cdo|701 nièng|ceb|701|ckb|٧٠١|crh|701|cs|701|cv|701|cy|701|da|701|de|701|el|701|eml|701|eo|701|es|701|et|701|eu|701|fa|۷۰۱ (میلادی)|fi|701|fo|701|fr|701|frr|701|fy|701|ga|701|gan|701年|gd|701|gl|701|he|701|hi|701|hr|701.|ht|701 (almanak jilyen)|hu|701|hy|701|id|701|ilo|701|io|701|is|701|it|701|ja|701年|jv|701|ka|701|kaa|701|kk|701 жыл|ko|701년|la|701|lb|701|lij|701|lmo|701|lt|701 m.|lv|701. gads|map_bms|701|mdf|701|mg|701|mhr|701|mk|701|mr|इ.स. ७०१|mrj|701 и|ms|701|myv|701 ие|mzn|۷۰۱|nah|701|nap|701|nds|701|new|सन् ७०१|nl|701|nn|701|no|701|nrm|701|nso|701|oc|701|or|୭୦୧|os|701-æм аз|pl|701|pnb|701|pt|701|qu|701|ro|701|ru|701 год|rue|701|sa|७०१|scn|701|sd|701ع|sh|701.|shn|701|si|701|simple|701|sk|701|sl|701|smn|701|sq|701|sr|701|su|701|sv|701|sw|701|tg|Соли 701|th|พ.ศ. 1244|tk|701|tl|701|tly|701|tr|701|tt|701 ел|uk|701|ur|701ء|uz|701|vec|701|vi|701|war|701|wuu|701年|xmf|701|zh|701年|zh_min_nan|701 nî|zh_yue|701年|qid=Q23496}} (Taihō 1) at {{ill|Hiruga|Q113625481|qid=Q113625481|lt=Hiruga}}, present {{ill|Mihama, Fukui|Q629384|qid=Q629384}}, then moved to the foot of Kanemukai-yama in Uenodani, and moved again to the current site in {{ill|806|Q30021|qid=Q30021}} ({{ill|Daidō|Q1373191|qid=Q1373191}} 1).

In Hiruga tradition, a fisherman named Rokurōemon of the village was fishing on the lake when a cormorant appeared and told him that a noble person was at the bottom of the lake seeking rescue. Led by the bird into the lake, he found a treasured sword on the lakebed, brought it home, and enshrined it on his household altar. Ugayafukiaezu-no-Mikoto then appeared in his dream and told him to enshrine him by the upper lakeshore and to name the village “Hyūga,” the name of his own land. The shrine name Uwase derives from “Uwase” (upper shoal).

Another tradition says that in the Taihō era, {{ill|Ugayafukiaezu|Q1373935|qid=Q1373935|lt=Ugayafukiaezu-no-Mikoto}} came from {{ill|Hyūga Province|Q513737|qid=Q513737}} in Kyushu, passed through {{ill|Izumo Province|Q582846|qid=Q582846}}, crossed the {{ill|Sea of Japan|Q27092|qid=Q27092}}, and appeared here. The Hiruga area is thought to have had migration from Hyūga in ancient times, and many dialect forms and place names are shared with Hyūga.

=== Medieval / early modern ===
In the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}, it is listed as a {{ill|Myōjin Taisha|Q9610964|qid=Q9610964}} and is the only one among 352 shrines on the {{ill|Hokurikudō|Q3139239|qid=Q3139239}} route to receive offerings for {{ill|Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|Q11516161|qid=Q11516161|lt=monthly}} and {{ill|Niiname-no-Matsuri|Q11501518|qid=Q11501518|lt=new harvest}} rites.

The shrine buildings were destroyed by warfare twice, in the {{ill|Kenmu|Q1193970|qid=Q1193970}} and {{ill|Genki (era)|Q1145064|qid=Q1145064}} eras.

=== Modern / contemporary ===
When {{ill|Namekata Kyūbei|Q128852094|qid=Q128852094}} dug the Urami River connecting Lake Suigetsu and Lake Kugushi in the {{ill|Kanbun (era)|Q1146228|qid=Q1146228}} era (1661-1673), he prayed at Uwase Shrine and the difficult engineering work succeeded. He arranged donation of two tan of rice fields as shrine land and personally dedicated a {{ill|Chōzubachi|Q2972160|qid=Q2972160}} stone basin<ref>{{Cite book|和書|author= |title=100 Notable People of Fukui Hometown |publisher=Fukui Prefecture |date=2017 |page=65 |isbn=}}</ref>. This basin is still placed in the precincts<ref name="若狭国での被害">"[https://www.bousai.go.jp/kyoiku/kyokun/kyoukunnokeishou/rep/1662_kanbun_omiwakasa_jishin/pdf/1662-kanbun-omiwakasaJISHIN_08_chap4.pdf Chapter 4: Damage, land change, and disaster response in Wakasa Province]" in ''Report (1662 Kanbun Ōmi/Wakasa Earthquake)'', Cabinet Office</ref>.

In {{ill|Kuantan Singingi Regency|Q7626|qid=Q7626}} ({{ill|Kaei|Q1146125|qid=Q1146125}} 4), the present shrine buildings were constructed.

On April 24, 2015, it was recognized as part of the Japan Heritage "Wakasa exchange cultural heritage linking sea and capital - Miketsukuni Wakasa and Saba Kaidō"<ref>{{Cite web|和書|url=https://japan-heritage.bunka.go.jp/ja/stories/story005/ |title=Wakasa exchange cultural heritage linking sea and capital |publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs |accessdate=2020-09-19 }}</ref>.

=== Festivals ===
* April 8 (one-month-late observance for lunar March 8) - Annual festival with dedication of dengaku, Ō-no-mai, lion dance, and Urayasu dance<ref name="文化遺産データベース">{{Cite web|和書|author= |year= |url=https://bunka.nii.ac.jp/db/heritages/detail/159558 |title=Ritual performing arts of Uwase Shrine |publisher=Agency for Cultural Affairs |accessdate=2015-11-29}}</ref>.
